title: "Resourcing"

# Overview

Analyzing questions related to future prospects for OSPOs.

Research questions:\
What does the next two years hold for OSPOs?\
Where are OSPO staff working to grow?

Survey questions:\
Over the next two years, what do you expect to happen to your OSPO or OSPO-like function?\
What is the time horizon of your current funding or allocation?\
Which areas do you expect to become more important for your OSPO over the next two years?\
Which area would you most like to grow, and what is stopping you?\
What skill or expertise do you most wish you or your OSPO had more of?\


# Import packages, utilities, and config variables
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)

source("utils.R")

# Read config.yml
cfg <- config::get()
```

# Load data
```{r}
mc_simple <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "mc_simple.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
org_responses <- read_excel(file.path(cfg$curated_path, "orgs.xlsx"), sheet="responses")
future <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "future_areas.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
ospo_loc <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "ospo_location.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
codebook <- read_excel(file.path(cfg$data_path, "codebook.xlsx"))
mc_complex <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "mc_complex.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
qual <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "qual.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
```

# What does the next two years hold for OSPOs?

```{r}
table(mc_simple$expectations)
```

```{r}
table(mc_simple$funding_duration)
```

Just for my own reassurance, I want to run some chi-square tests on some variables that I suspect might be correlated.

```{r}
# Expectations vs Funding
chisq.test(mc_simple$expectations, mc_simple$funding_duration)

# Expectations vs Formalization
chisq.test(mc_simple$expectations, mc_complex$function_mc)

# Funding vs Formalization
chisq.test(mc_simple$funding_duration, mc_complex$function_mc)
```

Well, the last one is bordering on significant, but it's the least interesting of the three relationships.

```{r}
tmp <- cbind(mc_simple$expectations, ospo_loc)
names(tmp)[1] <- "expectations"
tmp |> filter(tto == "Yes")
tmp |> filter(library == "Yes")
```

Hmm. I'm forming a hypothesis that OSPOs associated with a TTO are in better shape than those associated with libraries. Let's create an "optimism" score. "Optimists" this their department will either grow or stay the same.

```{r}
tmp2 <- tmp |>
  mutate(
    optimistic = expectations %in% c("Grow (more staff, funding, or scope)", "Stay about the same"),
    group = ifelse(tto == "Yes", "TTO", "Non-TTO")
  )|>
    select(c(optimistic, group))

head(tmp2)
```

```{r}
tmp2 |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    optimistic_count = sum(optimistic, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_optimistic = round(100 * mean(optimistic, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )
```

Meh, not sure if that's a significant trend. Let's test it.
```{r}
chisq.test(tmp2$group, tmp2$optimistic)
```

Nah.

## What areas will be important for OSPOs in the coming years?

I see one person gave all NA responses to this question. I will remove them. Nobody else gave any NAs.

count_yes_responses(future)
